profile.reading:
This building is a UPS facility at an address on McFarland Parkway in Alpharetta, Georgia, part of the North Fulton and Forsyth County corridor north of Atlanta that has grown since the 1990s into one of the region's denser concentrations of corporate back office, technology, and telecommunications real estate. UPS, formally United Parcel Service, is the world's largest package delivery company by volume, headquartered in Sandy Springs, Georgia, a short distance south of Alpharetta, and the company operates substantial technology infrastructure in the metro Atlanta area to support package tracking, logistics optimization, and the various customer facing and internal systems that keep its delivery network running globally.

UPS does not publish a dedicated public page describing this specific building, and no square footage, power capacity, construction date, or tenancy information for this address was located in the company's own newsroom materials or on its corporate site. That is consistent with how UPS treats its operational technology infrastructure generally. The company's public communications focus heavily on its delivery network, sustainability commitments, and corporate financial results, while data center and back office facilities used to run those operations are rarely singled out by address in press materials, unlike UPS's package sorting hubs and air cargo facilities, which the company frequently promotes publicly because of their direct relevance to service capacity and customer facing operations.

Companies in UPS's position generally treat core IT infrastructure as an operational cost center rather than a public facing asset, and there is little commercial incentive to publicize the physical characteristics of a facility that exists purely to support internal systems rather than to serve outside customers or tenants. Forsyth County property and permit records could in principle confirm details such as building size, year built, and ownership, and are typically searchable through the county tax assessor's office for readers who want to verify ownership independently. Based on the available evidence, this building is best understood as part of UPS's broader corporate technology footprint in the Alpharetta area, functioning as internal infrastructure for a large logistics company rather than as a commercial data center offering capacity to outside customers.

reading.body:
UPS operates this facility in Alpharetta as internal infrastructure to support its logistics operations, not as a commercial data center available to outside customers or tenants. The company does not publish power capacity, floor space, construction date, or any technical specification for this address. Without published figures, the facility's relevance to AI infrastructure scaling cannot be quantified.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish power capacity totaling 66.3 megawatts. This facility is ranked fifth in the state by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects the absence of a published figure rather than a measured capacity. It remains one of the vast majority of mapped facilities nationwide that disclose nothing about their infrastructure to the public.

Readers evaluating AI infrastructure constraints should note that most corporate technology facilities operated by logistics, finance, and telecommunications companies remain wholly opaque in their published specifications. This facility exemplifies that opacity. The power consumption that matters to grid constraints at the state level is concentrated among the small number of operators who choose to publish, while the aggregate footprint of unpublished internal infrastructure is unknown.
